diagrams.title: Economic dispatch with transmission loss
diagrams.cap: With losses, each generator runs where its incremental cost multiplied by its penalty factor equals the same λ. The penalty factor 1/(1 − ∂P<sub>L</sub>/∂P<sub>i</sub>) is above 1 for a unit whose output increases the losses, so that unit is loaded less than equal incremental costs would suggest.

diagrams.title: Y-bus, DC load flow and Kron reduction
diagrams.cap: Build Y<sub>bus</sub> by adding each element's admittance to the two diagonal entries and subtracting it from the off-diagonal pair. DC load flow drops resistance and takes |V| = 1, so P = B′θ is one linear solve; Kron reduction removes a bus with no injection and is just series–parallel reduction in matrix form.
diagrams.qq: Line of x = 0.2 pu between buses 1 and 2. Y₁₂?

diagrams.title: Power–angle curve & equal area criterion
diagrams.cap: Fault during δ₀→δ<sub>c</sub>: accelerating area A₁. After clearing: decelerating area A₂. A₂ > A₁ stable · A₂ = A₁ critical (limit) · A₂ < A₁ unstable (fault here gives P<sub>e</sub> = 0).

formulas.name: Equal area criterion
notes: Where: A<sub>acc</sub> = accelerating area (P<sub>m</sub> above P<sub>e</sub>), A<sub>dec</sub> = decelerating area available
Tip: Transient stability of single machine–infinite bus (SMIB). Critical clearing angle is found by setting the areas equal.
Example: Pm = 0.6 Pmax → δ₀ = 36.87°; a bus fault (Pe = 0): cos δcr = (π − 2δ₀) sin δ₀ − cos δ₀ ≈ 0.313 → δcr ≈ 71.8° — clear the fault before this angle.

notes: Where: C<sub>i</sub> = cost of unit i, P<sub>i</sub> = its output, P<sub>L</sub> = transmission loss, λ = incremental cost (₹/MWh), L<sub>i</sub> = penalty factor
Tip: Unit commitment decides which units run; hydrothermal scheduling uses limited water to cut fuel cost.
Example: ∂PL/∂P₁ = 0.2 → L₁ = 1/0.8 = 1.25; dC₁/dP₁ = ₹4/kWh becomes an effective ₹5/kWh, so plant 1 is loaded less than in the lossless dispatch.

f: real off-nominal tap keeps Y<sub>bus</sub> symmetric, a phase-shifting
notes: Where: N = number of buses, N<sub>PV</sub> = number of PV buses; k = the bus being eliminated
Example: 10 buses, 3 PV: Jacobian order = 2(10 − 1) − 3 = 15. Kron, removing bus 3 with Y₁₁ = −j8, Y₁₃ = j4, Y₃₃ = −j6: Y₁₁′ = −j8 − (j4)(j4)/(−j6) ≈ −j5.33.

formulas.name: Swing equation in degrees
notes: Where: G = machine rating (MVA), H = inertia constant (s), f in Hz, P<sub>a</sub> = accelerating power (MW), δ in electrical degrees
Example: 100 MVA, H = 5 s, 50 Hz, Pa = 20 MW: M = 100 × 5/(180 × 50) ≈ 0.0556 MJ·s/deg; d²δ/dt² = 20/0.0556 = 360 elec-deg/s² = 180 mech-deg/s² (4-pole).

Tip: Q flows from higher to lower voltage magnitude. Asked: GATE 2020 (Q57) · GATE 2018 (Q32) · GATE 2017-1 (Q64) · GATE 2022 (Q56) · TNPSC PG Q58.

formulas.name: Rotor oscillation frequency (small disturbance)
f: synchronising coefficient P<sub>s</sub> = P<sub>max</sub> cos δ<sub>0</sub> (pu/rad)
notes: Where: H = inertia constant (s), ω<sub>s</sub> = 2πf

why.cause: faster fault clearing → smaller rotor swing → transient stability ↑
inertia H ↑ → slower swing → more stable
why.effect: Large machines ride through disturbances better.

why.cause: Newton–Raphson: fewer iterations, more work per iteration than Gauss–Seidel
why.effect: N-R is preferred for large systems.

why.cause: load ↑ → f ↓ → primary control (governor droop) stops the fall
why.effect: Frequency settles a little below 50 Hz.

why.cause: secondary control (AGC, integral action) → f back to exactly 50 Hz
why.effect: Load-frequency control; tie-line power also held at schedule.

why.cause: real power ↔ frequency · reactive power ↔ voltage
governor (LFC) → P and f; excitation (AVR) → V and Q
why.effect: The two loops are nearly independent (P–f and Q–V decoupling).

why.cause: double circuit → X ÷ 2 → P<sub>ss</sub> = EV/X × 2 → steady-state stability ↑
why.effect: Clearing time, reclosing and inertia act only on TRANSIENT stability.

mistakes.c: Steady-state limit = EV/X only. Fast clearing improves TRANSIENT stability.
NR converges quadratically in a few iterations; GS is simple but slow.

mistakes.m: The equal area criterion applies to any multi-machine system
mistakes.c: It is for one machine against an infinite bus (or two machines).
